_source: The ring the levels place round a no-portal field, redrawn every frame by its own callback:
ETHCallback_antiportal (AntiPortalManager.angelscript, bytecode bytes 335020..335206, Enhanced's
out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0). A callback is named for the
entity less its .ent (ETHASUtil.cpp:63-67), so both spellings of the 71 placements run it:
ins 1-25   blinkColor(thisEntity, _portalColorA, _portalColorB, 300). A call pushes its last argument
first, so ins 1 pushes the stride 300, ins 4-8 copy _portalColorB and ins 12-16 _portalColorA.
ins 27-34  AddToAngle(g_timeManager.unitsPerSecond(10f)); ins 27 PshC4 1092616192 is 10f.
_portalColorA and _portalColorB are that file's own globals (initialisers at bytes 306547..306598 and
306617..306668). Each pushes 0f, 0f and then 0.2f (PshC4 1045220557) or 0.4f (1053609165) into vector3,
and a call pushes last-first, so they are vector3(0.2, 0, 0) and vector3(0.4, 0, 0): red. They are the
ANTIPORTAL's colours; a static portal's are static_portal's above, from another callback.
blinkColor(entity, colorA, colorB, stride), utilEntityEffect.angelscript bytes 326140..326616:
ins 1-25   the uint 'blinkElapsedTime' is set to 0 when the entity has none yet: the first call
ins 26-41  AddToUInt('blinkElapsedTime', g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime())
ins 43-53  elapsedTime = GetUInt('blinkElapsedTime')
ins 55-61  invert = (elapsedTime / stride) % 2 == 1 (DIVu, MODu 2, CMPIu v1, TZ)
ins 63-67  bias = float(elapsedTime % stride) / float(stride)
ins 69-75  bias = invert ? 1 - bias : bias
ins 77-90  SetColor(interpolate(colorA, colorB, bias)), where interpolate(a, b, t) = a + (b - a) x t
(Interpolator.angelscript bytes 314616..314759)
So the red is a TRIANGLE: 0.2 at 0 ms, 0.4 at 300, 0.2 at 600. A period is two strides.
THE TWO CLOCKS ARE NOT THE SAME ONE. blinkColor adds g_timeManager.getLastFrameElapsedTime()
(STimeManager.angelscript bytes 7894..7961), which is uint(float(GetLastFrameElapsedTime()) x
m_factor): ins 3 the engine call, ins 5 uTOf, ins 8 MULf m_factor, ins 9 fTOu. It is NOT capped at 200;
unitsPerSecond (bytes 8045..8162, ins 3-18) is speed x min(200, frame ms) / 1000 x m_factor, which is
(ins 5 pushes the 200, ins 9 calls min; motions.json's linear_motion.frame_cap_ms, the one the port
keeps). Both are capped at 1000 ms by the loop itself (Min(1000.0f, ComputeElapsedTimeF(video)),
android/main.cpp:180-181). m_factor is 1 and pause() sets it to 0, so both stand still under a pause,
and they part company only on a frame longer than 200 ms.
AND THAT CLOCK IS A FLOOR OF EACH FRAME'S MILLISECONDS, SUMMED AS A uint - which the port reproduces
since planning step 147 (sim/ScriptClock, clock.json). The Android loop measures a frame as a float of milliseconds (ComputeElapsedTimeF, gs2d
Application.cpp:36-50, off clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC): AndroidGLES2Video.cpp:66-69, so the fraction
is real and not a timer's quantum) and ETHEngine::Update stores static_cast<unsigned long> of it
(ETHEngine.cpp:147). THE SHIPPED LIBRARY DOES EXACTLY THAT: in libApplication.so
gs2d::ETHEngine::Update(float) at 0xb4100 calls ETHDrawableManager::RemoveTheDead (+0x0e), then
__aeabi_f2uiz at 0x1cb364 (+0x14) and ETHScriptWrapper::SetLastFrameElapsedTime(unsigned long) at
0xf2038 (+0x18). The C++ scene keeps the float (ETHEngine.cpp:166); what the SCRIPT reads is that
truncated uint (uint GetLastFrameElapsedTime(), ETHScriptWrapper.generic.cpp:323,
ETHScriptWrapper.System.cpp:100-107), and blinkColor sums it into the entity's own uint
blinkElapsedTime. So at a steady 60 Hz the original's blink clock gains 16 ms a frame, not 16.667, and
a 600 ms triangle takes 625 ms of wall clock; the script's second truncation (ins 9 fTOu) changes
nothing while m_factor is 1, since uint(16 x 1.0f) is 16. unitsPerSecond reads the same integer, so the
TURN is slow by the same factor. BUILT in planning step 147: the level's age, which this blink reads,
gains the script's 16 ms a tick (the engine's tick is 16.667 and drives the physics alone), so the 600 ms
triangle is 37.5 ticks, 625 ms of wall clock at 60 Hz. Before it, the port's blink and turn ran
16.667/16 = 4.17 % fast of the original's and reached opposite phase after 450 ticks (7.5 s).
WHAT IS DRAWN. SetColor writes m_v4Color's rgb and keeps its alpha (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498), and the sprite
is drawn at min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117). All 71 placements carry
emissive (1, 1, 1) (antiportal.ent's EmissiveColor), so that term is 1 on every level, chapter 4's dark
ones too, and the ring is drawn at the blink's own colour, added (antiportal.ent blendMode 1). No placement
carries an eth_color, so writing the rgb and multiplying it in are the same here; the port writes it.
AddToAngle adds to m_angle (ETHEntity.cpp:444-447, ETHEntityController.cpp:145-148), which the draw turns
the picture by (ETHRenderEntity.cpp:105, :122), counter-clockwise on the screen; the converter wrote each
node's angle negated (tscn.py:432-433).
antiportal.ent is static=1, so the original runs this callback only while the ring's bucket is on screen
(00_order 8.12c): it starts a ring's blink and its turn from the frame it is first seen. The port runs
every one from the level's first tick, as it runs motions.json's placed pictures (a recorded divergence).
The phase the original starts at also rests on the INFERRED immediate 1 in ins 58; no still can show it.

_source: What a depth the script writes as a raw number is, among the level's art (step 76). The original draws
by depth alone (ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:70-72 sorts every piece by ComputeDepth of its z; equal
depths keep the order they were added in, :74, :85, :106). Every entity the level file places is
multiplied by the scale factor at load: Game::preLoop instruction 37 calls SGlobalScale::scaleEntities
(bytes 6838..7228), which runs scaleEntity (bytes 6072..6337) on every entity not marked scalable 0, and

included. What a script adds at a literal z is not: AddEntity keeps the position it is given
(ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:131-158). So the player's 4 and a minion's 2 are depths in the world's
units, and a level node at eth_z k stands at k x scale_factor. In the level's units, where the port
draws: the player at 4 / 2.8125 = 1.42, between the one node at eth_z 1 (level22a) and the 54 at 2;
a minion at 0.71, after every node at 0 or below and before that one. 00_order 8.12b had left this
open as INFERRED ('raw literals versus scaled offsets'); the scaleEntity multiply decodes it.

callers each run it before the entity is first drawn: ETHCallback_key #117 (the block #1-12 enters while it
has no 'speed', its first update),
ETHCallback_keyhole #1-32 (while it has no 'elapsedTime') and ETHCallback_door_locked #1-19 (while it is not
'painted'). GetEntityName is the name as the level spells it (ETHEntity.cpp:309-312), so a placement spelled
key.ent would ask for key.ent_blue.png, which does not exist; none of the 24 blue or red pieces is spelled
so (test_mp_sprites pins it). key_blue.png, key_red.png, keyhole_blue.png, keyhole_red.png,
door_locked_blue.png and door_locked_red.png all ship in entities/, each with an hd twin of twice its
texels, the same size as the yellow file: 3-13, 3-14, 3-17, 3-21, 3-23 and 3-30 hold a yellow set and a
blue one, 4-01 a red keyhole and door, 4-19 a red key, 4-20 a red set. SetColor writes m_v4Color's rgb and
keeps its alpha (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498); no placement carries an eth_color, so white changes nothing drawn
today and is written as the script writes it. The sim already pairs them by this same datum
(Keys.cpp:141). The library's 3-13_h6.3 shows the blue keyhole, key and door where the port drew gold.
crateCallback (ETHCallback_crate.angelscript, bytecode bytes 421145..421695) #1-7 calls
manageNonTeleportable(thisEntity, zeroEmissive) (MiscCallbacks.angelscript, bytes 343765..344140) before
anything else. Its callers pass zeroEmissive as a constant (00_order 8.0 rule 1: SetV1 v1, v0 is 0 and
SetV1 v1, v1 is 1): ETHCallback_crate, _crate_small and _wood_piece_small pass 0, ETHCallback_crate_no_emissive
and _crate_small_no_emissive pass 1 (bytes 423812..424324). crate_low_emissive has no callback.
manageNonTeleportable: #1-10 unless isTeleportable, #11-21 unless isBurned (the uint 'burned', bytes
419817..419918), then #23-49 with zeroEmissive blinkEmissive(this, vector3(0.5, 0, 0), V3_ZERO, 600) and
#50-73 without it blinkColor(this, vector3(1, 0.3, 0.3), V3_ONE, 600). A call pushes its last argument first
(00_order 8.0 rule 3): #26 and #51 push the stride 600, then colorB (V3_ZERO / V3_ONE), then colorA, and
a vector3's own constructor takes z first, so #35-37 (0, 0, 0.5) is x 0.5 and #60-62 (0.3, 0.3, 1) is
(1, 0.3, 0.3): red both ways. isTeleportable (bytes 343470..343661) is GetUInt('teleportable') != 0, and
its second test, 'nonTeleportable', answers 0 too, so a crate with the datum absent is not teleportable;
Portals.cpp:871-873 reads the same datum the same way. blinkColor and blinkEmissive
(utilEntityEffect.angelscript, bytes 326140..327057) are one triangle: the entity's uint
'blinkElapsedTime' from 0, gaining the frame's time, and colorA + (colorB - colorA) x bias, bias the
remainder of a 600 ms leg over 600, turned back on odd legs (art.json antiportal has the listing). So
the colour runs (1, 0.3, 0.3) -> white -> (1, 0.3, 0.3) over 1200 ms, and the emissive (0.5, 0, 0) ->
0 -> (0.5, 0, 0). SetColor writes m_v4Color's rgb (ETHEntity.cpp:493-498), SetEmissiveColor the
emissive (:482-485), and the sprite is drawn at min(1, ambient + emissive) x m_v4Color per channel
(ETHRenderEntity.cpp:113-117). Once burned the blink stops: manageBurnable (bytes 420664..421145) then
writes the colour, not the emissive, which keeps the blink's last value.
